Die musikalische Bewertung nutzt den Ori: Musical analysis uses the original mix as a mono signal. For each display step, CLAP compares up to ten seconds of audio around its midpoint; context is shorter at song boundaries.
CLAP vergleicht Audio- und Textrepräsent: CLAP compares audio and text representations. Two English sound descriptions represent each of six emotion directions. Their logits are averaged in pairs, then normalised to relative similarities using softmax.
Jede relative Ähnlichkeit wird mit einem: Each relative similarity is multiplied by a fixed valence weight. Their sum gives Audio Mood between −1 and +1. This mapping is a development choice, not a scientifically calibrated emotion scale.

Modelltrennschärfe = 1 − H(scores) / ln(: Model discrimination = 1 − H(scores) / ln(6). Similar scores mean low discrimination. This is neither an accuracy rate nor the probability that your feelings are correct.
Tempo, RMS-Energie und spektrale Helligk: Tempo, RMS energy and spectral brightness are measured separately using librosa. They do not directly enter the CLAP valence formula. CLAP may consider rhythm, timbre or harmonic patterns, but this does not reveal which property caused an individual rating.
Es werden keine gesicherten Akkorde, Ton: These values do not establish chords, keys or instrument personnel. Vocals, noise and the selected descriptions may affect the estimate. Player colours visualise these estimates.
Pro Audioabschnitt werden überlappende L: For each audio section, overlapping Lyric Mood values are averaged using their overlap duration. At least half the section must have lyric coverage. The largest absolute difference from audio valence is marked; the percentage is difference / 2 × 100.
Colours follow Audio Mood and Lyric Mood. Motion follows playback and stored RMS energy; this is not a live frequency spectrum.
